rationale: A 2026 Oakland planning table identifies this parcel with Alameda County use code 1000, which the County defines as residential vacant; a 2016 county environmental report also calls it a vacant, unpaved lot. A secondary source dates demolition to Jan 2015. This supports a vacant parcel, though the exact start and uninterrupted duration are not proven.
duration_note: About 11 years 8 months since reported demolition; official documentation confirms vacant land by 2016-05-03. Continuous vacancy after those observations is likely but not directly verified.

evidence.source_name: Alameda County Environmental Health / Stellar Environmental Solutions, Site Development Strategy, 1125 Mandela Parkway
evidence.detail: Describes the exact property as a 10,000-square-foot vacant, unpaved parcel. It also identifies it as a former 1957–approximately 1969 service station.

evidence.source_name: City of Oakland Planning Commission, 2026 zoning comparison attachment
evidence.detail: Lists 1125 Mandela Pkwy, APN 004 006300601, and Alameda County use code 1000. Alameda County's vacant land survey defines use code 1000 as Residential Vacant. This is an assessor classification, not direct proof of physical condition on the observation date.

evidence.source_name: Alameda County Farm Bureau, Ashland Cherryland Vacant Land Survey Report
evidence.detail: Defines Alameda County Assessor use code 1000 as Residential Vacant. Used only to interpret the code shown for this APN in Oakland's 2026 table.

evidence.source_name: Alameda County Assessor property history, parcel 4-63-6-1
evidence.detail: Identifies 1125 Mandela Pkwy and shows assessor use 4000, matching the county environmental report's description of county code 4000 as Vacant Industrial. Historical record only; it does not establish current occupancy.

evidence.source_name: Oakland LocalWiki, It Only Takes a Pair of Gloves Mural
evidence.detail: Reports that the building and mural at 1125 Mandela Parkway were demolished on January 29, 2015 for environmental cleanup. Community-edited secondary source; use as a likely start date, not sole proof.

limitations: The 2026 use code is an assessor classification, not direct onsite observation; no evidence located establishes the exact physical condition or uninterrupted vacancy throughout the period.
This finding concerns the parcel/building site and does not imply a residential unit was vacant for the entire period.
